newsitem.title: FRANCE: French banks chief raps reluctance to reform.
newsitem.headline: French banks chief raps reluctance to reform.

text.p: The chairman of the French banks' association AFB accused political authorities on Tuesday of reluctance in implementing major reforms of the banking sector, long dogged by weak profitability.

Reiterating a call for an end to competitive distortions in the sector, Michel Freyche deplored what he called the "nervousness of political authorities and their hesitation in taking the decisions necessary".
He made the comments in a speech to the group's annual dinner attended by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis.
Freyche said a Senate report last month urging sweeping changes constituted "the indispensable basis for all deep reform" of the sector.
Among its recommendations, the report called for changes to tax and labour laws, greater transparency in the financial activities of the Post Office and restructuring of a range of savings products.
But Freyche said that the AFB did not share all of the Senate committee's conclusions.
The Senate report also blasted the banks for years of "tatical or strategic management errors".
